newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-GREEK IOC MEMBER TIPS ROME, ATHENS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-GREEK IOC MEMBER TIPS ROME, ATHENS.

text.p: A Greek IOC member tipped Rome and Athens on Thursday as the strongest candidates from a shortlist of cities who are bidding to host the 2004 Olympic Games.
But Lambis Nikolaou, who arrived at Rome's Fiumicino airport on Thursday on an official visit to examine the bid, said the outcome would not sour relations between the two countries.

"I believe that Rome and Athens have presented the best credentials to be able to win in 100 days' time. The best candidate will win and whatever happens, we will remain friends," Nikolaou told reporters.
The International Olympic Committee is due to make its final decision on September 5 from a shortlist which also includes Stockholm, Cape Town and Buenos Aires.

Nikolaou, in Rome for four-day visit, was accompanied by Swiss IOC member Rene Fasel. FIFA president Joao Havelange said during a visit to Rome earlier this month he thought a European country would win the bid.
